lines.text: This week, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's letter to staff about affair,
and developers are scrambling to benchmark their clusters.
Sending shockwaves across the entire AI hardware market.
For years, companies poured billions into GPU farms,
assuming hardware speedups would continue without limits.
Then engineers discovered a surprising software bottleneck.
Instead of blaming memory bandwidth or thermal limits,
they analyzed the kernel execution pathways.
The result? Benchmarks revealed extreme speed variance
across server workloads that usually run at peak compute.
With optimized kernels running up to seventy times faster,
saving millions in redundant server power,
and proving that software optimization beats raw hardware.
Engineers are calling this an urgent wake-up call for AI clusters.
Because the true speed of next-gen AI
depends on code architecture, not just trillion dollar chips,
